one_line: A 15-second hands-and-pumpkins demo from a toddler-activity expert showing a two-bin setup (paint bin, wash bin) where kids paint pumpkins, scrub the paint off, and repeat all fall.

hook.visual: Top-down shot of several children's hands painting three pumpkins in a clear plastic bin, with a muffin tin of saturated paints in the lower third. Orange, red, blue and white everywhere; no faces, only hands, brushes and one child's hair at the bottom edge. The shot opens mid-mess, i.e. the end state of the activity.
hook.on_screen_text: Burned-in word-chunk captions that mirror the voiceover. At 1.0 s: "you're". At 2.0 s: "going to do all fall". (No caption visible in the 0.0 s frame, so the first words "This is the activity" are not captured in the sampled frames.) (you're going to do all fall)
hook.first_spoken_line: This is the activity you're going to do all fall long. (same, English, per Whisper)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Observed: the first frame is a dense, colour-saturated top-down view of messy, happy hands, with no talking head and no intro. Inferred: it shows the payoff (kids absorbed in paint) before explaining how, and the spoken promise 'all fall long' sells a repeatable, season-long idea in the first 2.8 s.

payoff: The full recipe is delivered by about 12.8 s (two bins, washable paint, paint-wash-repeat). The emotional payoff is the smiley-faced pumpkin and 'makes kids so happy' at 14.0-14.8 s. There is no big reveal; it is a quick, complete how-to.
cta: None in the video itself. The caption ends with 'Share it, save it, try it' and opens with 'Don't sleep on this.'
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: a cheap, seasonal, no-skill activity that a parent can send to another parent or save for October. The caption pre-answers the obvious questions (washable paint source, bin size, 'yes the paint comes off'), which makes it save-worthy and reduces the need for comments. Comments are only 107 on 707,440 views (about 0.015%), so saves and shares, not discussion, are the likely driver; saves and shares are not in meta.json, so this is unverified.
why_it_worked: 707,440 views is 2.8x the account median of 248,562 with a like rate of 1.23%: a solid, above-median result for an account that already performs, not a freak outlier. The seasonal topic (posted 2026-09-29, start of pumpkin season) fits the repeatable, evergreen-in-October nature of the idea (inferred).

The very first frame is the most visual moment of the whole video (observed), and the whole video is 14.8 s with a new shot every 1 to 3 s and captions on every word chunk, so the recipe lands before attention drops (inferred).
The idea is a 3-step setup with everyday supplies and a built-in loop (paint, wash, repeat), which makes it feel doable and re-usable, and the caption carries the FAQ (paint, bins, washability).
paid_signal: no: like rate 1.23% is well above the 0.3% paid-pattern threshold and the outlier is modest at 2.8x; no ad label visible in the frames. The caption tags a school-supply brand (@discountschoolsupplies) for the paint, which could be a partnership or just credit; that cannot be verified from the frames.

solo_route.how: 1) Mount the phone on a tripod or a stack of books looking straight down at a table in daylight; shoot hands only, no faces, 3 short setups. 2) Open on the most colourful finished moment, then cut to a wide 'set up' shot and show the steps in order, one shot per instruction, 1 to 3 s each. 3) Record a 15 s voiceover yourself in CapCut, run auto-captions and set them to 2 to 4 word chunks in a single serif or clean font on a white pill. 4) Put the supplies and the FAQ in the caption and end with a save and share line.
solo_route.needs: For a LumeBook craft or making-of version: nothing beyond a printed sample book and your own hands. For a true kids' activity version like the original: a relative's or friend's child with written parental consent, and keep faces out of frame.

lumebook_version.concept: Top-down, hands-only making-of: open on the finished book spread with the illustrated child, then rewind to three steps (upload a photo on the phone, the free AI preview on screen, printed pages being trimmed and bound), with burned-in word-chunk captions and a short voiceover, plus an FAQ in the caption (how long, what you need). No faces, no kids on camera.
